newsitem.title: EGYPT: Faisal Bank of Egypt in 50 pct capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Faisal Bank of Egypt in 50 pct capital increase.

text.p: Faisal Islamic Bank of Egypt will raise its capital by a maximum of $50 million, a 50 percent increase that could let foreign shareholders own a majority stake, an executive at the bank said on Tuesday.
"The bank's general assembly has already approved the increase and letters will be sent to the shareholders in January or February,"the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The bank now has capital of about $100 million. Faisal Islamic Bank of Egypt has a complicated share structure, with some shares denominated in Egyptian pounds and some in dollars.
Bank sources earlier said they expected most of the capital increase to come from foreign shareholders, diluting the Egyptian shareholding to less than 50 percent.
An amendment to the Egyptian banking law earlier this year made it possible for foreign partners in joint-venture banks to own more than 51 percent of the equity in the banks.
The biggest foreign shareholders are Faisal Islamic Bank of Saudi Arabia and Geneva-based Dar al-Mal al-Islami, which is owned by Saudi interests.
The Bank said on Monday its net after-tax profits in the first half of the Islamic year 1417 rose to 166 million pounds ($49 million) from 142 million for the same period a year ago.
The first half of its financial year ended on November 11, 1996.
The bank does not pay interest which is forbidden in Islam. Its shares are listed on the Egyptian stock exchange in Egyptian pounds and U.S. dollars.
